decisions.executionNote: Approach the green-handled crimper with the right arm, beginning a continuous downward wrist rotation while keeping the left arm stationary.
Retry the approach with half-size increments after the zero-motion IK rejection, preserving elbow configuration.
Continue toward the right-side crimper with the open gripper, rotating downward gradually and maintaining clearance.
Move above the crimper while raising the wrist slightly to keep the descending fingers clear of the table.
Continue the overhead approach with the right gripper open; preserve clearance while completing the downward pitch.
Finish pitching the gripper downward above the green handles, without lowering toward contact yet.
Rotate the open jaws around the vertical tool axis so they can pinch across the crimper handles; remain above contact.
Continue the in-place jaw alignment above the crimper; no descent until the jaw direction is established.
Complete the vertical-axis rotation so the jaws close across, rather than along, the green handles.
Lower the aligned open gripper cautiously toward the handles, using the head and wrist views to check fingertip clearance.
Make a small centering correction and descend another 15 mm to place the open fingertips around the handle region.
Close the right gripper around the handle region at fixed height; retention will be checked visually during a small lift.
Keep the gripper closed and perform a cautious 3 cm test lift, checking whether the crimper moves with the fingers.
Continue lifting vertically with the right gripper fully closed, observing whether the crimper clears the tabletop rather than slipping.
The crimper remained on the table during the test lift. Reopen and return toward it for a deeper grasp rather than assuming retention.
Lower the open jaws farther around the handles for a deeper second grasp; keep the same lateral alignment and watch for contact.
The descent shows contact resistance. Back off 3 mm, close the jaws at this deeper level, and pause before testing retention.
Keep the deeper grasp position fixed and maintain a fully closed command to allow the fingers to settle before lifting.
Test the settled deeper grasp with a slow 3 cm vertical lift, keeping the gripper commanded fully closed.
Continue the second lift while holding fully closed; monitor the crimper’s motion and any drooping or slipping at the handles.
The crimper is visibly tilting with the grasp. Raise it another 5 cm with the jaws closed, allowing clearance for its hanging head.
Lift the retained crimper another 5 cm, keeping the wrist orientation steady and the jaws closed to compensate for the tool hanging below the grasp.
